focus.name: focus-ring
focus.purpose: Keyboard focus on buttons, links, inputs, toggle; offset 2px on page-level primary actions.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Tailwind default; colour transitions on links, tabs, buttons and the toggle knob slide. Nothing else animates.

drift: Page title size: Dashboard 32px, every other view 24px.
Focus rings vary: login inputs ring 2px, search and page-size select ring 1px; CopyButton button variant uses focus (not focus-visible) and font-medium; dialog danger confirm rings in fail red.
Mark colours are hard-coded hex in BrandMark.vue and favicon.svg rather than tokens.

fonts.purpose: All UI text; chosen for legibility and continuity with gatecha.org. Detector overused-font ignore for Inter is sanctioned.
Counts, key IDs, secrets, version, chart axes.

narrative.overview:
The admin answers one question before anything else: does any of my sites have a problem right now? Every surface is built around that order. Failing keys are named first with their counts, then today's verification funnel, then every key grouped by what the admin has to do about it, then the 30-day history. When nothing fails the page says so in one line, and it says nothing about keys working until a verification has actually happened today.

The world is GateCHA's own, shared with gatecha.org: a light header band (white with a bottom hairline; panel colour in dark mode) carrying the teal shield mark and the two-colour wordmark, over the slate-grey ground the site uses (a night ground in dark mode). Inter sets every word and Overpass Mono tabular figures set every count. Structure is drawn with 1px hairlines; there are no drop shadows anywhere. The GateCHA teal is the one brand colour and carries actions, links and focus; green, amber, red and grey are reserved for state. The density is that of an operations table: 14px body, 10px row padding, panels inset 20px, and the numbers lead.

Brand history: on 2026-10-24 the owner rejected the transit metro metaphor, then a navy band with a yellow "G" mark, and kept GateCHA's teal and shield. Neither rejected identity is to be re-proposed, nor replaced by another borrowed metaphor.
keyCharacteristics: Attention first: failing keys open the page and sort first in every list.
One brand identity with gatecha.org: teal shield mark, "Gate" + teal "CHA" wordmark, slate neutrals, Inter.
Hairline panels on a tinted ground; no shadow, no gradient, no decorative colour.
Counts in Overpass Mono with tabular figures, formatted `en-US`.
Light and dark both designed, following the system theme through the same token names.
Self-hosted fonts only; nothing loads from a third-party host.

rules.name: The One Teal Rule
rules.body: Teal means "you can act here or this is GateCHA": actions, links, focus, the mark and the wordmark. It is never used for state, and green is never used for an action.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, red and grey mean verified, failing, failed and disabled, and nothing else. They never decorate. The one standing exception is text selection, which borrows the amber.

rules.name: The Words-First Rule
rules.body: Colour backs a word, it never replaces one. Every status chip spells OK, No traffic, Failing or Disabled; every sparkline carries an aria-label; a disabled key's trend is dashed as well as grey.

rules.name: The Same Names Rule
rules.body: Dark mode redefines the same custom properties under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`. Components use semantic tokens only and never branch on the theme. Text pairs are meant to hold 4.5:1 on ground, panel and sunken in both themes; strokes and marks 3:1.

rules.name: The Light Weights Rule
rules.body: Bold (700) is for page titles and the wordmark only; panel headings, names, labels, chips and buttons are semibold (600). No extrabold or black anywhere.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every count is set in Overpass Mono with `tabular-nums` and formatted with `toLocaleString('en-US')`. No bare `toLocaleString()`, no proportional digits in a column.

rules.name: The UTC Rule
rules.body: "Today" is the current UTC day and every date is formatted in UTC (`en-US`, short month and day). The dashboard title says "(UTC)".

rules.name: The Attention-First Rule
rules.body: Failing keys come first everywhere: named in the banner, first group in the keys panel, rank 0 in sorting (failing, OK, no traffic, disabled). A key is failing when today it has at least 5 failures and those are at least 20% of its verifications.

rules.name: The Honest Quiet Rule
rules.body: "All keys are working today." appears only when today has verifications. With active keys but no verification yet, the line reads "No verification yet today." in muted text on a plain panel.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px rules: panel borders and the band edge in rule, row separators and chart gridlines in rule-soft, controls in rule-strong. No shadow cards.

dos: Do name failing keys first, with failed-of-verified counts, before any chart.
Do use the four statuses OK, No traffic, Failing, Disabled from `lib/status.ts`, always as words, with colour behind them.
Do set every count in Overpass Mono with `tabular-nums` and `toLocaleString('en-US')`.
Do set UI text in Inter at 400 to 700: bold for page titles and the wordmark, semibold for headings, names, labels and controls.
Do draw structure with 1px hairlines (rule, rule-soft, rule-strong) on panel over ground.
Do use semantic tokens only, so dark mode follows by redefining the same names.
Do keep the shield mark one drawing across `BrandMark.vue`, `public/favicon.svg`, gatecha.org and the WordPress.org assets.
Do say "today" in UTC and format dates in UTC.
donts: Don't bring back the metro metaphor, the navy band or the yellow "G" mark, nor any other borrowed metaphor: no numbering keys, no per-key colours, no themed status vocabulary.
Don't use teal for state or green for an action.
Don't use green, amber, red or grey for anything but state.
Don't use extrabold or black weights.
Don't add drop shadows or shadowed cards.
Don't say keys are working before any verification has happened today.
Don't use flag emoji for countries; use the ISO code tag.
Don't load fonts, scripts or images from a third-party host.
